content.introduction: The sources describe an earnings calendar as a schedule of when publicly traded companies report their financial results, typically quarterly. Platforms like Zacks Investment Research and Investing.com aggregate this information to help investors track multiple companies at once. The calendar is a strategic investing tool that allows investors to plan trades ahead of volatility, compare expectations vs. reality, track trends across sectors, use predictive tools, and monitor post-earnings reactions. The Investing.com Earnings Calendar tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide, displaying EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results. The Markets Insider Earnings Calendar allows tracking of companies releasing earnings reports, sorting by market cap, and accessing historical data and earnings news.

## What are Earnings?

Earnings refer to a company’s profit, usually measured as earnings per
share (EPS)—the portion of profit allocated to each outstanding share
of stock.

### Why companies must report earnings (legal requirement)

## FAQ

### What is the Investing.com Earnings Calendar?

The Earnings Calendar is a free tool that tracks earnings report dates for publicly traded companies worldwide. It displays EPS and Revenue forecasts alongside actual results once released, so you can compare analyst expectations with reported outcomes in a single view.

### What is an earnings surprise? [...] Most publicly traded companies report earnings four times a year, once per fiscal quarter. Earnings season typically begins a few weeks after each quarter ends, with the busiest reporting periods falling in January, April, July, and October. Not all companies report on the same date, so the Earnings Calendar helps you track which companies are reporting on any given day.
